title: Controls on SIM cards and GSM gateways used for scam calls
asked: Victor Lye asked whether the Government will consider tighter controls and real-time anomaly detection for bulk SIM card purchases, SIM re-registration patterns and GSM gateway misuse, which let overseas scam calls appear local.
response: Tan Kiat How set out existing upstream controls: since 1 October 2025 scam mules are barred from subscribing to new mobile lines, and from 28 February 2026 each person is limited to 10 postpaid SIM cards across all telcos, on top of the existing cap of three prepaid SIM cards. IMDA, GovTech and SPF use data analytics to detect suspicious SIM card purchase and registration patterns, and GSM gateways with five or more SIM card slots require IMDA's prior approval for import since 1 February 2025. In 2025, SPF disrupted more than 105,000 scam-related mobile lines. He said thresholds are reviewed across agencies and refined as scam tactics evolve, and that operational details are not shared for security reasons.

key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How

key_points.quote: because of operational security considerations, we do not want the bad actors to know what we are doing

key_points.point: Cases with SMS as the first contact method fell about 65%, from 1,285 cases in 2024 to 450 cases in 2025.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: The number of cases with short message service (SMS) as the first contact method has also decreased about 65% – from 1,285 cases in 2024, to 450 cases in 2025.

key_points.point: IMDA and GovTech developed a tool, SIMCardHowMany, for mobile users to check the number of postpaid SIM cards registered under their names.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: IMDA, together with GovTech, has jointly developed a new tool, SIMCardHowMany
